coverageMatrix.completeness: Cephalosporin alone covers ~80% of non-purulent cellulitis; add MRSA-active agent if purulent or risk factors present.
gaps: MRSA not covered by cephalosporins alone - add only with purulence or specific risk factors, not routinely.

stewardship.deescalation: If culture (from purulent component) identifies MSSA, narrow from broader MRSA-active agents to a cephalosporin. If no purulence and clinical improvement is seen, no escalation is needed regardless of culture status.

drugs.dose: TMP-SMX 160/800 mg PO q12h or Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h
drugs.coverage: Added or substituted when purulence or MRSA risk factors are present, since cephalosporins do not reliably cover MRSA.

framework: MRSA coverage should not be added by default for non-purulent cellulitis - reserve for purulent disease, abscess, or specific MRSA risk factors.

Crepitus, bullae, severe pain out of proportion to exam findings, or rapid progression should prompt urgent surgical consultation to rule out necrotizing fasciitis rather than antibiotic escalation alone.
Mark the border of erythema at presentation to objectively track response and avoid premature escalation for expected initial spread.

references: IDSA Skin and Soft Tissue Infection Guidelines
